scope: 46 endpoint statements reviewed for conceptual consistency; targeted source verification, not laboratory validation or an exhaustive validated SOP.

practice.matrix: Hypothetical dilute aqueous nitrate salts, acidified with nitric acid. Five target cations, not five total ionic species.
practice.compatibility: Chemically reasonable teaching scenario by solubility reasoning; no physical mixture was prepared or experimentally validated. Avoid specifying unverified concentrations.
practice.caution: Nitric acid introduces nitrate; nitrate confirmation on this prepared solution cannot prove an independently unknown original anion.

corrections.text: Black deposit requires Sn–Ag contact couple; a black deposit alone is insufficient. Gilreath adds NaOCl insolubility discrimination against arsenic.
Accept white OR gray precipitate, not mandatory visible white-to-gray sequence.
White, gray or black endpoints depend on reduction extent; do not reject gray/black simply because transient white was missed.
Gilreath alcoholic reagent gives blue-green junction; Birk acetone variant gives blue liquid. Label protocol variants explicitly; omit cobalt photo for a junction question.
SCN detects Fe(III) in test portion; oxidizing preparation does not establish original iron oxidation state.
Iron masking/removal is necessary when Fe accompanies Ni.
Timing is essential: delayed arsenate sulfide can imitate yellow arsenite product. Photograph alone cannot distinguish.
Arsenate interference requires specified treatment. A white precipitate is not the yellow positive endpoint.
Flag both positive results in the same acid-prepared group as a consistency conflict: chlorate and nitrite react.
Require nitrite removal and interference control; endpoint is conditional, not unique in untreated mixtures.
Keep historical reference-only; no definitive positive branch for current practical identification.

logic_requirements: Retain liquid after a positive group precipitation.
Separate independent portions; do not run all confirmatory reagents in one tube.
Uncertain and skipped are not negative.
Invalidate descendant answers after earlier preparation changes.
Element identification after redox is not original oxidation-state assignment.
